headline: Tk 90cr road caves in months after completion in Gazipur
summary: A nearly one-kilometre stretch of the Rajabari-Damdama road has subsided, with locals alleging poor construction quality.
details: A newly constructed 5.5-kilometre road in Gazipur’s Sreepur upazila has subsided along a nearly one-kilometre stretch just a few months after its completion.
The Rajabari-Damdama road, built at a cost of around Tk 90 crore, is reportedly collapsing towards the Suti river due to poor construction work, according to local residents.
The project was awarded to Messrs Salam Traders in 2021 and was completed earlier this year, though it was originally scheduled for completion in 2024.
Local residents report that the road has suddenly started sinking with large cracks appearing, and they are calling for an investigation to hold those responsible accountable.
Md Touhid Ahmed, an LGED engineer in Sreepur, stated that a six-member team from higher authorities has recently inspected the damaged section.
The LGED engineer noted that immediate repairs are not possible during the ongoing monsoon, but 10 percent of the security deposit from the contractor has been retained.
Investigations into allegations of irregularities in the road construction are ongoing, and action will be taken against the contractor if the allegations are proven.
Abdus Salam, the proprietor of Messrs Salam Traders, acknowledged that parts of the road have subsided and promised to repair the damaged portions.

The project was awarded to Messrs Salam Traders in 2021 and was completed earlier this year, though it was originally scheduled for completion in 2024.

Local residents report that the road has suddenly started sinking with large cracks appearing, and they are calling for an investigation to hold those responsible accountable.

Md Touhid Ahmed, an LGED engineer in Sreepur, stated that a six-member team from higher authorities has recently inspected the damaged section.

The LGED engineer noted that immediate repairs are not possible during the ongoing monsoon, but 10 percent of the security deposit from the contractor has been retained.

Investigations into allegations of irregularities in the road construction are ongoing, and action will be taken against the contractor if the allegations are proven.

Abdus Salam, the proprietor of Messrs Salam Traders, acknowledged that parts of the road have subsided and promised to repair the damaged portions.

headline: 14 children killed as tuition center roof collapses in Lahore
summary: A tragic incident in Pakistan's Lahore has left 14 children dead after the roof of a learning center collapsed.
details: A devastating roof collapse at a tuition center in Lahore, Pakistan, has resulted in the death of 14 children.
Rescue workers and locals rushed to the scene to pull survivors and victims from the rubble of the building.
The incident has sparked concerns over the safety and structural integrity of small-scale private educational centers in the city.
Emergency services are working to clear the debris and ensure no one else remains trapped under the collapsed structure.
